landing.heroTitle: Discover which occupations fit your skills
landing.heroSubtitle: Tell us about your background and skills in your own words. We'll show you the occupations your experience fits best — and the concrete skills to develop to get closer to your goal. A clear picture of your career path in minutes.
landing.feature1Body: You don't need to know thousands of skill terms. Tell us about your background and we'll do the mapping for you.
landing.feature2Body: Get a ranked list of occupations your skills fit best — and a percentage showing how close you are.
landing.feature3Body: Clearly see which skills you already have and which are worth learning next.
landing.trustNote: Built on the EU's official ESCO v1.2.1 occupations and skills classification.

langfit.title: LangFit – language requirements, task by task
langfit.subtitle: Paste a job ad. LangFit splits the job into tasks and records, for each, which language is needed, at what level and when – from day one or within 6–12 months. You get a posting text, a rationale note and a language plan.

intro.step1Body: The job is split into 5–10 concrete work situations.
intro.step2Body: Per task: a CEFR level for four skills, a timeline and a job-based reason.
intro.step3Body: Outputs are generated only from rows the employer approved.

notice.title: AI suggestions are labelled – LangFit describes the job, it doesn't assess people
notice.body: Rows produced by AI are marked “unvalidated” and are not saved until the employer approves them. AI can't remove the statutory requirement of a regulated profession. This is a demo: nothing here is legal advice, and the legal references must be checked.

onboardPath.title: Onboarding Path – from new hire to skilled professional
onboardPath.subtitle: Choose the role you are hiring for and the new hire's previous occupation. Onboarding Path shows which skills are already in place, what is learned at the workplace and which qualification units cover the rest.

intro.step1Body: Two ESCO occupations: the new role and the previous one.
intro.step2Body: Missing essential skills learned together with a work buddy.
intro.step3Body: As few Finnish qualification units as possible to cover the remaining gaps.

notice.title: Compares occupations – doesn't assess people
notice.body: The path is computed directly from the ESCO classification and the Finnish National Agency for Education's ePerusteet; no language model is used. It describes the difference between two occupations, not anyone's personal skills: confirm actual skills in a conversation with the new hire. Demo – check the terms of training and funding.

picker.title: Create an onboarding path
picker.hint: The previous occupation is optional. Without it, the path covers all essential skills of the role.
picker.toHint: E.g. warehouse worker, cook, healthcare assistant.

phase2.hint: Missing essential skills with no matching qualification unit. Learned on the job with a buddy or a responsible person.

phase3.title: Qualification units
phase3.hint: As few Finnish qualification units (tutkinnon osat) as possible to cover the remaining essential skills. They can be completed while working, e.g. as an apprenticeship.

phase4.title: Later
phase4.hint: Optional skills of the role not found in the background. A good next step once the basics are in place.
